candidates.object: Fixed-point fractional-grid transport for PR837 bidirectional Horner
candidates.method: Exact 2-adic valuations of every coefficient and whole-program primitive prefix; integer-grid counterexamples

candidates.reason: The source explicitly discloses missing exact dual certificates; a further solver audit would need a separate larger scope

statement: Exact endpoint equality and positive magnitude-prefix bounds do not alone establish preservation of the old fixed-point fractional grid. Quantify the extra grid depth for the actual PR837 choices and all six pinned programs. This audits an explicitly unresolved precision obligation, not a claim of a defect in the selected construction.
method: Prove the necessary/sufficient denominator-depth criterion for dyadic linear prefix maps. Census all 962 coefficients, replay all six original and replacement programs and produce exact integer-rounding witnesses with corrective guard bits.
domain: The scalar primitive projections of fixed #626 CK/JP8 and #741 SW4 programs bound in PR837, both orientations, arbitrary native/private input columns. Fixed dyadic grids; exact intermediate representability, not physical frame/phase evaluation or all-size numerical stability.
stopping_rule: Complete this finite census and replay; no compiler integration, exponent repricing or exploratory search beyond the stated domain
expected_finish: Approximately 90 minutes from the claim; final quarter for validation and handoff
coordination: Local claim; only issue #650 requested Discussions at previous refresh; no sprint coordination issue available.

result.statement: CK forward scalar-projection fractional guard rises from 3 to 5 bits under PR837; shared forward/backward guards remain CK=8, JP8=27, SW4=19.
result.whole_program_counterexample: CK forward, native basis column 16: endpoint errors at guards 3 and 4, exact at guard 5.
result.precision_scope: Fixed dyadic-grid representability of the scalar projection; physical frame/phase/recursive realizations and integer overflow outside scope.
